line: A good plan can survive one person getting tired, one tool failing, one assumption being wrong, or one experiment going badly.
brief: Chad calmly works beside a modular scaffolded project with several independent supports while one tired teammate sits down, one tool lies broken, and one failed component has been removed; the overall work remains stable and continues without drama.

line: A system may discover a better method. That does not mean it has earned the right to deploy that method, widen its own permissions, or remove the gate that judged it.
brief: A powerful machine presents an improved mechanical part toward a sturdy external gate, while Chad outside the machine retains the separate key and inspection lever; the better part is visibly useful but cannot install itself or open the gate.

line: A person hears a potentially embarrassing truth and remains standing.
brief: Chad stands relaxed and steady while another person points out a plainly visible flaw in a project on the workbench; instead of shrinking, posturing, or arguing, he calmly looks at the flaw and stays composed.
